issues.description: No regression test for the stack-reuse bug this PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The PR claims it fixes non-zero elements in the stack slice when a Sorter is reused, but ships no test. A bug fix without a failing-before/passing-after test is on the honor system. Add a test that calls Sort twice on the same Sorter and asserts the second run is clean and produces identical output.

issues.description: Semantic change to s.state[k] = sorted write is unjustified and undocumented.
issues.detail: Previously every pop unconditionally wrote sorted; now the write only fires inside the state != sorted branch. The values are likely equivalent, but the commit message says nothing about it and the invariant on pop becomes state becomes sorted unless already sorted. Either restore the unconditional write or document why the change is safe.

issues.description: Collapsed working/walking state and new defer-based cleanup lack a written invariant.
issues.detail: Merging working and walking into one state is a reasonable simplification, but the loop invariant and the meaning of each state are not stated anywhere. The previous distinction separated children-pushed from on-the-ancestor-path; readers must now reconstruct that cycle detection via push() still works. Add a paragraph naming the invariant and justifying why the merge is safe.

issues.description: Typos in the new comment: visisted and if its.
issues.detail: The rewritten comment introduces visisted (should be visited) and if its (should be if it's). The surrounding file holds a literate-programming standard; fix the spelling before landing.

issues.description: Three logical changes bundled into one diff without separate justification.
issues.detail: The PR description lists three fixes: state reduction, stack-slice cleanup, and state-clearing on completion. Each is independently bisectable and the commit message does not justify why the working/walking merge is safe. Split into separate commits or expand the message to explain each change.

issues.description: Sorter complects per-call traversal state with reusable identity, making defer-clear necessary.
issues.detail: state, stack, and iterating live as mutable fields on Sorter shared across Sort() calls. The reentrancy panic and the defer-clear cleanup exist only because identity is complected with per-sort value. A Sort that returns iter.Seq over local scratch state (or uses sync.Pool) would eliminate both concerns. Not a blocker for this patch, but worth reconsidering.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches a clear NEEDS-WORK consensus: the change is small and directionally correct — collapsing working/walking, moving cleanup into defer, and fixing the yield/pop ordering are sensible — but it ships under-audited. Three reviewers want a regression test for the stack-reuse bug this PR claims to fix, a written invariant for the simplified state machine, and justification (or reversion) of the now-conditional s.state[k] = sorted write. Comment typos and the three-fixes-in-one-commit shape should be cleaned up before landing. Hickey notes the underlying design complects identity with per-sort value, but that is a follow-up, not a blocker.
